title: Fermented foods: promising, early
covers: Yogurt, kefir, kimchi, sauerkraut, miso and tempeh.
summary: An early Stanford study found a fermented-food diet raised gut microbial diversity. Experts say the health benefits aren't yet established.
in_our_recipes: Why kefir, kimchi and sauerkraut show up often, and why we add kimchi at the end of cooking to keep its live cultures.

sources.title: Marco et al., Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology 2021 (ISAPP)
American Gastroenterological Association: The gut microbiome
